budget_items.what_was_said: The principal assessor reported growth figures received from RRC for personal property, given as an assessed value and the corresponding tax dollars, described as growth only, not a new total.
A separate growth figure was given for the other property classes, described as being in valuation.
Combined growth in valuation was said to be roughly a figure that far exceeded an earlier estimate, credited partly to fieldwork finding previously unrecorded property.
The board signed the warrant for motor vehicle excise commitment number five, covering a stated number of bills and a total tax amount, for both the tax collector's and accountant's copies.

budget_items.topic: Interim value adjustments by property class (FY26)
budget_items.what_was_said: Vision's late interim adjustment figures were summarized: increases for single families, condos, two-families, three-families and the land curve, based on prior-year to current-year interim values and excluding growth.
The per-acre value used for excess or residual land beyond the prime site acreage was stated as unchanged from the prior year.

budget_items.topic: Seasonal temporary employee for neighborhood directive project
budget_items.what_was_said: Because no bids were received for the neighborhood directive project, the board discussed hiring a temporary/seasonal employee instead, to be added as a personnel item on the special town meeting warrant.

budget_items.topic: Clause 41A senior tax deferral income limit
budget_items.what_was_said: A warrant article for town meeting would raise the income limit for the senior tax deferral program from a fixed figure to one tied to the state circuit breaker credit's income cap, with some uncertainty about how the cap applies to married/head-of-household filers.

budget_items.topic: Chapter 61 rollback taxes / lien on land taken out of chapter land
budget_items.what_was_said: A property removed from chapter land after failing to file an application was returned to full value, and the owner remains liable for a period of back rollback taxes because a lien had been recorded.

budget_items.topic: Cost to record a chapter-land lien with the Registry of Deeds
budget_items.what_was_said: Recording a chapter-land lien costs a fee paid by check to the Registry of Deeds, not out of the assessors' office budget.

An estimate for a mapping software upgrade was described as a modest increase over current cost, but could not be pursued until fiscal 2027; the board wants more detail on field-mapping functionality and possibly other vendors before committing.

decisions.decision: Put establishing hardship criteria for Clause 18 tax relief on the agenda for the next meeting, before any application is reviewed.
Revise the executive session minutes language to read "the first two of a total of eight" applications reviewed, rather than implying all eight were reviewed.
Try to schedule an additional meeting the following week, tentatively Wednesday October 22 at 6:30pm, focused on reviewing interim adjustments.
Hold the tentative classification hearing on November 25 or December 2, pending approval of the LA-3/LA-15 submission.
Send the board's drafted response to the master planning committee covering exemptions and chapter land programs.

The board will hold off on any action regarding the chapter-land property under a purchase-and-sale agreement until the Select Board's first-right-of-refusal process and open space committee review progress further.
Add a code-of-conduct document (modeled on one from Littleton) to a future agenda for discussion.
Have the principal assessor ask the town's IT/records contact whether board members can be granted access to a shared file system without each creating a separate account.
Prioritize meeting with any new applicants for the vacant board seat at the next meeting if scheduling allows.

minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors reviewed a lengthy, repeatedly late set of FY26 interim property valuation adjustments from vendor Vision, expressing frustration over years of missed deadlines and unclear report formatting while working to finalize sales data (LA-3/LA-15) ahead of a tentative late-November classification hearing. The board also discussed a prospective new board member applicant, a warrant article raising the senior tax deferral income limit to the circuit breaker cap, a chapter-land property under a pending sale, a possible GIS mapping software upgrade, and drafted a response to the town's master plan committee, before entering executive session to review FY26 exemption applications.

what_happened.line: The board reviewed late FY26 interim property valuation adjustments from vendor Vision, citing years of missed deadlines.
A classification hearing, which sets tax rates by property class, was tentatively set for late November or early December pending sales-data approval.
A warrant article would tie the senior tax deferral program's income limit to the state circuit breaker credit's income cap.
The board held off acting on a chapter-land property under a pending sale until the Select Board's first-refusal review proceeds.
Executive session minutes were corrected to state that only two of eight exemption applications had been reviewed, not all eight.

why_it_matters: Vendor delays in valuation data can push back the classification hearing that sets how the tax burden splits between residential and commercial property.
The proposed deferral change would let more seniors qualify to defer property tax payments, a warrant article residents will vote on at town meeting.
How the town handles the chapter-land property under agreement affects whether it exercises a right to acquire or restrict that land's use.
